title: Strict JSON parser: recovery heuristics and compatibility experiment
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: validate a strict JSON enforcement path that can 1) fail fast for schema violations, 2) gracefully recover partial streaming output without violating callers' contracts, and 3) emit telemetry that lets ops tune fallback policies. This ticket scopes an experimental testbed and a set of blackbox/whitebox tests to evaluate trade-offs between deterministic constrained decoders and probabilistic recovery heuristics when the model emits malformed or out-of-schema JSON during streaming and tool/function-calling scenarios.

Scope: build a harness that runs across three axes: (A) streaming partial output with injected token-level corruption, (B) tool-calling interleaved with JSON fragments, and (C) decoder fallbacks (strict reject, best-effort patch, allow-safe-keyword-rewrite). Measure: schema_violation_rate, fallback_latency_ms, recovered_tokens_ratio, and end-to-end client-visible error modes.

Non-goals: full product rollout or console UX changes. This is an infra/engine experiment focused on test coverage and metrics to inform a later rollout plan.
comments: 2026-02-15 - Kickoff: aligned with Runtime and Eval teams on metrics. Decided to prioritize streaming-first scenarios because most production incidents originate from partial responses during long generations.

2026-02-20 - Prototype PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3892. Prototype implements a thin compatibility shim that attempts bracket-balanced reassembly on partial streams before handing to the constrained decoder.

2026-02-23 - Early results: strict decoder rejects ~12% of synthetic corruptions, shim-reassembly recovers ~7% of those with a median +18ms decode penalty. Logged a higher-than-expected memory spike when reassembling very long KV caches; opened ENG-261108 to track memory regression.
2026-02-28 - PM review (Jordan Lee): requested explicit acceptance criteria for rollback behavior and clear guidance on customer-visible error messages. Added acceptance criteria below.

2026-03-03 - Design review (Lina Gomez): suggested a 'repair hint' field in telemetry so downstream UX can present precise remediation steps to integrators. We agreed to emit repair_hint but not change API surface yet.

2026-03-06 - Flakiness triage: intermittent failure when a tool call inserts newline-escaped JSON; added interleaved-toolcall scenario to the harness and a fix in the tokenizer boundary tests. Related issue: ENG-240711.

2026-03-10 - Current status: harness merged to local CI, unit tests passing 89% (failures are two edge cases for >8k token KV cache). Running 72-hour fuzz sweep on the fleet of small models in the staging cluster. Next: add long-tail telemetry dashboards and draft rollout runbook.

Notes and links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SO/Strict+JSON+Recovery+Experiment; Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/so/strict-json-experiment; Eval harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/feature/strict-json-experiment; Runtime prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3892
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness runs deterministically in CI and produces reproducible metrics for schema_violation_rate and fallback_latency_ms.
2) For seeded corruption workloads, at least one recovery heuristic must reduce customer-visible error rate by >=25% vs strict reject with <50ms median decode penalty.
3) Telemetry fields (repair_hint, schema_failure_reason, recovered_tokens_ratio) are populated for all fallback events.
4) No regression in tail memory usage for typical KV cache sizes (<=2MB).
next_steps: Complete fleet fuzz sweep (infra ticket created), finish long-tail telemetry dashboards, produce runbook with rollback triggers and recommended defaults for canary deployments, and present findings at next weekly Runtime sync. Estimate additional 2 cycles to finalize heuristics and product integration.
